checks.name: CSV and JSON imports produce identical parsed records
All 30 invoice statuses, balances and assigned outputs match the declarative oracle
All five aggregate satoshi totals match fixed expected values
31 input rows yield exactly 26 distinct outputs and 5 ignored duplicates
Status distribution and exception count match the authored fixture
Reimporting the complete 31-row receipt file adds no payment credit
Two outputs from one transaction separately settle SYN-016
Equal amounts on a reused address leave one output unassigned
Zero and unknown confirmations remain pending without reducing outstanding
Excess payment does not offset a different unpaid invoice
A missing explicit invoice reference gives that output no credit
An explicit invoice reference with the wrong recipient gives no credit
A noted manual assignment credits only the selected invoice
Manual exclusion retains the note and gives no additional credit
Workspace restoration preserves sample labelling, decisions and accounting
JSON and CSV reports retain all 30 invoices and 26 output evidence rows
A conflicting duplicate rejects the merge without changing existing receipts

limits: All customers, invoices and transaction IDs are fictional.
This measures deterministic fixture outcomes, not merchant adoption or general accuracy.
Human review time and the proposed 50% improvement have not been measured.
Browser interaction and responsive UI checks remain unverified.
